findings.path: games-r3.md > Damage and armour maps > 'Tempest Rising armour' bullet (line 89); unit armour/class, armour/notes, uncertain armour/class
findings.summary: The Tempest Rising armour note says the infobox label alone decides the class. That overrides the soldier rule, which wins over every step. The Line Officer's game data gives him tougher infantry armour than the Field Scout, so he should be light, not unarmoured.
findings.evidence: Line Officer wiki infobox (wikitext via API; the page is verified at 1.4.0): armortype Infantry, with a quarter resisted against Rifle, Explosive, Fire and Sniper damage. Its changelog says the Sniper resistance was added in patch 1.2.0+46089. The Field Scout's infobox resists no Rifle damage and lists only the Rocket and Cannon resistances. The Dynasty Guard's matches the Field Scout's. The 2.0.0 patch page changes only his range. The soldier rule in vocabularies.md (armour-class tie-breaks) wins over every step: a soldier whose game data gives a tougher infantry armour type or attribute than the basic rifle infantry is light. The Generals note sets a gunfire test for this same rule, but the TR note instead says the label is enough. The unit's armour.notes says 'Step 1 decided ... the registry reads the class from that label'. j06 hesitations[17] and unclear_rules[2] report following the note against the rule. Other batch soldiers checked: the Drone Operator (infobox resists no Rifle damage) and the Enlightened (same) stay unarmoured.
findings.fix: games-r3.md line 89. Old: 'Units also have six armour percentages, but the label is enough for the class.' New: 'Units also have six armour percentages. For vehicles and aircraft the label is enough for the class. For the soldier rule, a soldier of the Infantry type has tougher armour than the Field Scout, and so is light, when its percentages let less Rifle or Sniper damage through than his (he resists neither). One that resists only Rocket and Cannon damage, as he does, stays unarmoured, and side-wide doctrines such as Body Armor stay out.' Recode tempest-rising.dynasty.line-officer: armour.class unarmoured -> light. Rewrite armour.notes to say the soldier rule decided: step 1 gave unarmoured, but he resists a quarter of Rifle and Sniper damage where the Field Scout resists none. Rewrite uncertain armour/class to name the note. No other batch unit changes.

findings.path: games-r3.md > Research notes > Generals > 'The 1.04 files' bullet, second sentence (line 372); units armament[].traits, armament[].delivery, related uncertain entries
findings.summary: The Generals note says any term only the 1.04 files would set is not set, with friendly-fire as its example. That contradicts the field rules. A damage radius or a travel speed in any page an uncertain entry names counts for splash and for projectile delivery, and a database page may carry a code. Coders followed the note, so four units lack terms the rules give them.
findings.evidence: fields.md sources[]: 'the sources' are the cited pages plus every page an uncertain entry names and says what it shows, and an uncited database page may carry a code. The splash rule in vocabularies.md: a radius figure in the sources counts. The delivery rule in fields.md: a travel speed in the sources makes a shot projectile. 1.04 Weapon.ini, fetched from TheSuperHackers repository at 6c7f40d: TechnicalRPGWeapon has PrimaryDamageRadius 5 and RadiusDamageAffects includes ALLIES. TechnicalCannonWeapon has radius 25 and ALLIES. SentryDroneGun has WeaponSpeed 600 and no projectile object. AuroraBombWeapon has radius 20 and ALLIES (NOT_SIMILAR). OverlordTankGun has radius 5/10 and ALLIES. Each unit's uncertain entries name Weapon.ini: Technical armament/0/damage and armament/2/summary, Sentry Drone armament/0/delivery, Aurora armament/0/range and armament/0/traits, Overlord roles/secondary. The coders say they followed the note against the rules: j02 hesitations[6] and unclear_rules[6], j04 hesitations[5] and [17], and the Aurora's uncertain armament/0/traits. Current codes: Technical armament[2].traits is [], armament[1].traits is [splash]; Sentry Drone armament[0].delivery is hitscan; Aurora armament[0].traits is [splash]; Overlord armament[0].traits is [splash]. The note's other examples agree with the rules: the magazine rule rejects a clip size alone, and mount is a proposal field.
findings.fix: games-r3.md line 372. Old: 'Any other term only they would set (friendly-fire from a blast that hurts allies, magazine from a clip size, auto-target from an add-on's own AI) is not set; mention the fact in notes.' New: 'A term whose own rule a figure or flag in these files meets is set from them as from any other page an uncertain entry names: splash from a PrimaryDamageRadius above zero, projectile delivery from a WeaponSpeed the file does not mark as effectively instant, and friendly-fire where a weapon with a damage radius lists ALLIES in RadiusDamageAffects. Any other term only they would set (magazine from a clip size alone, which its rule does not accept, or auto-target from an add-on's own AI) is not set; mention the fact in notes.' Recodes: generals.gla.technical armament[2].traits [] -> [splash, friendly-fire] and armament[1].traits [splash] -> [splash, friendly-fire]; drop the uncertain armament/2/summary clause about the radius not being coded. generals.usa.sentry-drone armament[0].delivery hitscan -> projectile, and rewrite uncertain armament/0/delivery. generals.usa.aurora-bomber armament[0].traits [splash] -> [splash, friendly-fire], and rewrite uncertain armament/0/traits. generals.china.overlord armament[0].traits [splash] -> [splash, friendly-fire] (its source set names Weapon.ini). Rerun the validator for any new atypical lines.

findings.fix: games-r3.md line 291. Old: 'Record it as a passive ability; no pattern or armour model covers it, so add a fit_note.' findings.path: generals.china.overlord countered_by/4
findings.summary: The Overlord's Jarmen Kell link stands alone on a false claim that no typed link fits. pattern:hijack-vehicle fits his crew snipe, so the generator never sees this counter.
findings.evidence: countered_by/4 is unit:generals.gla.jarmen-kell with no typed link beside it. Its why says it stands alone because a sniper link would be false for most snipers. But Kell's Sniper Attack (abilities/0) links hijack-vehicle, and his strengths/1 is pattern:hijack-vehicle. The Battle Bus codes the same snipe as pattern:hijack-vehicle plus the unit link (countered_by/2-3), and the Sentry Drone uses the same pattern (counters/1). The registry summary of hijack-vehicle: take over an enemy vehicle by throwing out or killing its crew. The cited Overlord wiki page (cached copy) has, in its Counters section, the GLA sending Kell to snipe away the crew and leave the tank open to capture. Under fields.md matchups rule 3, a unit link may stand alone only when every word-list and pattern link would be false for most units it covers. The fill hesitation (research/r3/fill/hesitations.md, Overlord countered_by) weighed only weapon:sniper. Unit links never reach a card, so the generator loses this counter.
findings.fix: Replace countered_by/4 with two entries, in this order: {"ref": "pattern:hijack-vehicle", "why": "A crew-killing snipe takes it out however thick its armour: Jarmen Kell kills its crew and leaves the tank neutral for enemy infantry to claim (wiki)."}, then {"ref": "unit:generals.gla.jarmen-kell", "why": "The same reason: the wiki names Jarmen Kell, whose snipe empties it."}. damage:emp moves to countered_by/6.

findings.path: generals.gla.battle-bus counters/0, counters/1 and uncertain at counters (against countered_by/2)
findings.summary: pattern:hijack-vehicle sits in both the bus's counters (Hijackers foiled) and its countered_by (Kell's snipe empties it), in the same loaded-bus situation. A generator reads 'beats' and 'is beaten by' for the same enemies.
findings.evidence: counters/0 is pattern:hijack-vehicle: since patch 1.03, Hijackers cannot take a loaded bus. countered_by/2 is pattern:hijack-vehicle: Kell's snipe kills the driver and the riders spill out. Both need riders aboard. Only the enemy unit differs, and the typed link cannot tell those units apart. Kell's Sniper Attack links hijack-vehicle, and Kell's counters/2 role:transport claims the bus. My scratch pair check (same matching logic as the validator) puts Kell in both of the bus's lists, with each claiming to beat the other. In Generals the hijack-vehicle units are the Hijacker, Kell's snipe and the Nuke Cannon's neutron shells (Sentry Drone strengths/2), and the bus foils only the first. Under fields.md, rule 6 allows the same enemy in both lists only for different situations. Rule 1 covers a link that covers units its reason is false for.
